newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ cabinet to press on with NZ$100 mln building.
newsitem.headline: NZ cabinet to press on with NZ$100 mln building.

text.p: New Zealand's cabinet opted to patch up differences over budgetary issues on Monday and forge ahead with plans for a new NZ$100 million government building adjoining parliament, Radio New Zealand reported.
It quoted Foreign Minister and former deputy prime minister Don McKinnon as saying the decision had been taken at the routine, weekly cabinet meeting during the day.
McKinnon said in a statement that government "had confirmed the decision to proceed with the construction of a new parliamentary building".

Discussions have been going at cabinet level for several weeks into whether the plan could still be justified in the light of the impending budget, and Treasurer Winston Peters requested a thorough review, McKinnon said.

Peters issued his own statement saying that after re-examining all the alternatives "we have gone for the most cost-effective option against a difficult background" of policy decisions by previous governments.
While he said he would have much preferred the money going into health care or education, he believed that as $11 million had already been spent, little could now be saved by stopping.
Both ministers said the government would look for ways to make further savings as the project goes forward into the tender stage by the middle of next month.
McKinnon said that while the cost of the building has been capped at $94 million, "the government will be keen to receive tenders that come in well below that figure".
